title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in Ards and north Down lost £250,000 in an AI generated scam, the Police Service of Northern Ireland said. The victim saw an AI generated video that seemed to feature a well known financial sector figure. It promoted an investment with large returns. After a small payment, the victim was contacted on WhatsApp and urged to pay more. The fraudsters got remote access to the victim's computer and had them open several accounts.

Police described it as a sophisticated and substantial fraud. The victim was encouraged to borrow money, and the funds went to accounts run by criminals. The PSNI did not name the celebrity. BBC News NI has seen similar scams using Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett. Police said a celebrity endorsement should not be taken as proof an investment is genuine. Superintendent Joanne Gibson of the Scamwise Partnership urged people to stop and check financial activity and to talk to relatives about fraud. Police advised verifying who they are dealing with and checking that financial services providers are authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority.
